title: Wilks' theorem as a regularity result
dek: Λ →d χ²_k under nesting and interior regularity. Complementary to stats-lrt, which already owns the lab how-to. Title avoids stealing that search.
story: Wilks' theorem on Wikipedia is the regularity result behind nested likelihood-ratio tests: twice the log-likelihood gap goes to χ² with degrees of freedom equal to the number of restrictions, when the truth is interior and information is well behaved.

stats-lrt already teaches nesting, the statistic, and TB-lab worked examples. This card is the named theorem, plus the boundary caveats the encyclopedia lists (variance components at 0, mixture weights) that phylogeny and random-effect TB models hit.
Samuel S. Wilks 1938 is citation-only. We do not ingest the paper.
deep: Testing σ²=0 is on the boundary: the null limit is a mixture of χ², not χ²_1.
Non-nested models are outside Wilks — Vuong or AIC, not a fake Λ.
Profile versus maximised likelihood in the presence of many nuisance parameters can break the simple χ² (incidental parameters).
Wald and score are first-order equivalent under the same regularity — sibling cards.

visual.caption: Schematic: a χ²-like reference the theorem promises under regularity, versus a more piled-up mixture you get on a boundary. Not a fitted density from data.
